_readme: Enrolled device public keys for the local docker-compose stack ONLY.
This document is the input to the approval signature check in
services/confirm/device_signature.py. Its format belongs to
postern_core.auth.device_keys; top-level keys other than 'customers' are
ignored, which is what lets this note live here.
IT ENROLS NOBODY, ON PURPOSE. The confirm service refuses to start without
a device key store, and this is the one line of configuration that says
'no phone can approve yet' -- there is no line of configuration anywhere
that says 'approve without checking'. Starting against it warns loudly
(postern_core.auth.device_keys's warn_no_enrolled_devices) and every
approval is refused with 'device_not_enrolled'. The compose stack has no
database wired into confirm, so it could not approve anything regardless.
NO PRIVATE KEY IS COMMITTED HERE, and a 'd' parameter in any entry below
is refused at startup rather than ignored: a device signing key that has
reached a file on a host is compromised. To exercise an approval locally,
generate a key pair, paste the PUBLIC half in, and sign the canonical
message with the private half you keep:
uv run python -c "from joserfc.jwk import OKPKey; import json; \
k = OKPKey.generate_key('Ed25519'); \
print(json.dumps(k.as_dict(private=True)))"
The bytes to sign are postern_core.auth.approval_signature's
canonical_approval_message, built from the stored challenge row.
